To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
miRNAs are able to target the CDS and 5′-UTR regions of their mRNA targets, and that this is an important regulatory mechanism for the expression and function of many genes.

the microRNA miR-29c-5p is a key player in the regulation of the expression of a large number of genes involved in the regulation of cell cycle and cell proliferation, and that miR-29b-3p and miR-29a-5p also play a significant role in this regulatory mechanism.
miRNA-target interactions can be predicted with high confidence from a combination of CLIP-seq data and expression profiles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the miRNA targets and the miRNA-mRNA interaction network, which is a key step in understanding the miRNA regulatory network.
the development of an algorithm that is able to detect miRNA targets in CDS.
the development of a new method for the detection of miRNA target genes based on the integration of CLIP-Seq datasets and expression profiles of miRNA and their potential targets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
microRNA target sites in CDS are not as abundant as in 5’UTR regions.
the miRDB database is a useful tool for miRNA target prediction, miRNA functional analysis, and miRNA target site discovery.
miRNA-target interaction is a complex process and the prediction of miRNA target sites is a challenging task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the miRanda algorithm has a higher accuracy than other methods in predicting microRNA targets in the CDS regions, and that miRanda is more accurate than the other algorithms in predicting microRNA binding sites in the 5′UTRs.
MtiBase provides an integrated platform that combines the most up-to-date information on miRNA-target interactions with the expression data of miRNAs and their targets.
we have developed a database for decoding the microRNA target sites in the 5′UTRs and CDS regions of genes, which is based on the combination of CLIP-Seq data and expression profile data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
miRNA-mediated repression of gene expression can occur in the CDS of a gene.
the majority of miRNAs target sites in CDS regions are not conserved and are not predicted by conventional algorithms.
microRNAs can have a major influence on the expression of genes located in their own genomic neighborhood.
